note: lz-string 1.5.0 does the compressing. CyberChef's Compression Format (default, UTF16, Base64) is the format choice, with uri (compressToEncodedURIComponent) added. The result is bytes: Forge text cannot hold lone surrogates, which the default format's 16-bit units often contain (CyberChef shows that string as UTF-8, which cannot round-trip), so default is the units as UCS-2 big-endian byte pairs, exactly the library's compressToUint8Array; utf16 is compressToUTF16 written as UTF-8; base64 and uri are ASCII. The input is UTF-8 text (anything else is E_COERCE). The compressed values equal the library's.

The same formats as Compress, and the same representation of the default format (an even number of bytes, E_COERCE otherwise). Empty input, a truncated stream (no end marker), a code naming no dictionary entry, a wrong alphabet and decompressed text that holds an unpaired surrogate are E_COERCE (the library returns null or an empty string for several of these). The format expands quadratically, so before the library runs a replay of the token structure with lengths only stops at the value limit with E_LIMIT_VALUE; a 4 MB bomb of a few KB is refused in milliseconds. The vectors come from the library itself: no independent implementation could be run locally.

The LZ4 frame format written from the specification (no library; CyberChef uses lz4js, whose frame has independent 4 MB blocks and a content checksum, which are this op's defaults apart from level). Parameters added: level (0 stores, 1 to 9 a greedy hash-chain matcher following up to 2^(level-1) candidates; default 1), block-size (64KB to 4MB), independent, block-checksum, content-checksum and content-size. The bytes differ from lz4js and the lz4 command, but both read them (240 option combinations checked with lz4 v1.10.0 -d).

Frames (version, flags, block sizes; independent and linked blocks; stored blocks), with the header checksum, block checksums, content checksum and content size verified by default (verify; off recovers damaged data). Concatenated frames are joined, skippable frames are skipped and legacy frames (0x184C2102) are read; a dictionary id, an unknown magic number, trailing bytes that are not a frame (as the lz4 command rejects them) and cut-short data are E_COERCE. Output past the value limit is E_LIMIT_VALUE; the content size is never used to size a buffer. Raw (frameless) blocks, which CyberChef does not offer either, are not supported.
